# 🔥 LinkedIn Jobs Scraper

The Apify actor [`bebity/linkedin-jobs-scraper`](https://apify.com/bebity/linkedin-jobs-scraper) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.226**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

ℹ️ Designed for both personal and professional use, simply enter your desired job title and location to receive a tailored list of job opportunities. Try it today!

## Pricing

Pay per event — Actor Start $0.00005, Job result $0.0015, ⭐ Company & hiring-contact insights $0.001, ⭐ Company website $0.0009 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/bebity/linkedin-jobs-scraper) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/bebity-linkedin-jobs-scraper@0.0.226#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `titles` | array |  |  | Job titles / keywords — What to search for (e.g. Web developer). Add several — each is searched separately (up to Results per search each) and every result is tagged with the term it came from (in scrapingInfo). Leave empty for a broad search. |
| `locations` | array |  |  | Job locations — Where to search (e.g. Paris, New York). Every title is crossed with every location — each title × location pair is its own search — and every result is tagged with the location it came from (in scrapingInfo). |
| `rows` | integer |  | `0` | Results per search — How many jobs to return per search (up to 1000). Each job title × location is its own search. Set 0 (the default) for all available — every search runs to its last page. The whole run is also capped by the max items / cost limit you set on the run, so use that to bound the total |
| `companyName` | array |  |  | Company name — Restrict to specific companies by name (e.g. Google, NASA). |
| `companyId` | array |  |  | Company id — Restrict to specific companies by numeric LinkedIn id (e.g. Facebook: 76987811, Uber: 1815218). Numbers only. |
| `companyUrls` | array |  |  | Company URLs — Filter the search to specific companies by their LinkedIn page URL (e.g. https://www.linkedin.com/company/openai/) — often easier than finding the numeric id. Combines with your title/location filters. A numeric /company/{id} URL is used directly; a name URL is resolved automatically. |
| `publishedAt` | string |  | `""` | Published at — How recent the posting must be. |
| `easyApply` | boolean |  | `false` | Easy Apply only — Only return jobs that offer LinkedIn Easy Apply. |
| `under10Applicants` | boolean |  | `false` | Under 10 applicants — Only return jobs with fewer than 10 applicants — less-competitive roles. |
| `workTypes` | string[] |  |  | Workplace type — On-site, Remote and/or Hybrid. Pick one or more to match any of them. |
| `contractTypes` | string[] |  |  | Employment type — Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Temporary, Internship or Volunteer. Pick one or more to match any of them. |
| `experienceLevels` | string[] |  |  | Experience level — Internship → Director. Pick one or more to match any of them. |
| `industry` | string[] |  |  | Industry — Filter by company industry — pick one or more from the list (no ids to look up). Combine several to match any of them. Filtered accurately on Linkedin’s side. |
| `startUrls` | array |  |  | LinkedIn URLs — Paste LinkedIn job-search URLs (from the search page after applying filters), single job URLs, or a company page URL (e.g. https://www.linkedin.com/company/openai/) to scrape every job at that company. When provided, these drive the run and the search filters above are ignored. |
| `maxRowsPerUrl` | integer |  | `0` | Max results per URL — Maximum results to collect from each pasted URL above. Set 0 (the default) for all available — each URL runs to its last page. Bound the total with the run's max items / cost limit. |
| `companyProfile` | boolean |  | `true` | 🏢 Company profile — Add each company's profile to its jobs: headcount, followers, industry, description, tagline, headquarters (structured), company type, founding year and the company's website. Read once per company from its public LinkedIn page and reused across that company's jobs. Turn it off  |
| `enrichCompany` | boolean |  | `false` | ⭐ Hiring contact & job signals — Add the fields the listing card does not carry: the hiring contact's headline and photo, the salary source (employer-provided vs LinkedIn estimate), and the job's own signals — workplace type, job status (open/closed), exact posting timestamp, repost flag, verified-h |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
